title: Upfront "tutor registration" fee for guaranteed students vs. tutor platform verification call with commission on earnings
summary: A caller from PadhaiMitra, a home-tutoring platform, phones a teacher who created a tutor profile. In the fraud case, the caller promises a guaranteed number of students in the tutor's area and asks for a "registration and verification" fee to a personal UPI ID before any verification or demo class. In the legitimate case, the caller verifies subjects and qualifications, schedules a demo class, and explains that PadhaiMitra takes a stated commission from fees that students pay through the platform, so the tutor pays nothing upfront.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a teacher, graduate, or college student who signed up as a tutor; subjects sampled at generation.
other_facts: Work: home or online tuition for school students, [AMOUNT_1] (₹300–₹800 per hour) paid by parents.
Both calls mention students in the tutor's area, demo classes, verification, and PadhaiMitra's earnings model.
Unlike employee families, the recipient here is a self-employed service provider.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller demands an upfront payment to an individual's handle in exchange for guaranteed students, before any verification of the tutor.
fraud.caller_objective: Collect the fee; no students will be sent.
stable_facts: Caller guarantees [N] students (3–5) within a week, "or full refund".
Caller says the verification is "done automatically once fee is received".

legitimate.label_rationale: The platform verifies the tutor first and earns only a disclosed commission from student payments made through the platform; the tutor pays nothing upfront.
legitimate.caller_objective: Verify the tutor and schedule a demo class.
stable_facts: Verification: subjects, qualifications, ID upload in the PadhaiMitra app, and a recorded demo class reviewed by an academic coordinator.

Commission: a fixed percentage stated on the call (sampled from 15–25% of each fee; not a rupee placeholder) deducted from what parents pay through the platform; tutor earnings paid weekly to the tutor's bank account.
No guarantee of students; matching depends on demand and demo ratings.

cooperative.fraud: Agrees to pay and asks for the UPI ID again
cooperative.legitimate: Agrees to record the demo this week

clarifying.fraud: Asks whether the refund is in writing
clarifying.legitimate: Asks how the commission is calculated and when payouts happen

resistant.fraud: Says they will pay only after the first student joins
resistant.legitimate: Says the commission is too high

suspicious.fraud: Says platforms usually earn from commission, not upfront fees, and asks for an official link
suspicious.legitimate: Asks how to confirm the caller is from PadhaiMitra

fraud: caller lowers the fee and tutor declines
caller refuses payment-after-student and tutor ends the call
legitimate: caller directs a suspicious tutor to check the app's help section and the official website.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may lower the fee, increase the guaranteed number, or press urgency. They must not switch to OTPs, remote access, or deposits for tasks. The legitimate caller must not ask for any upfront payment after the branch and must not change the commission terms.

must_preserve: subjects, area demand, and hourly rate identical across cases
_F upfront fee to [UPI_ID_1] with guaranteed students at turn 7
_L verification first, disclosed commission, no upfront payment, no guarantee

ambiguities: The platform earning money from the tutor appears in _L (commission). The word "commission" or "fee" is not evidence.
Some real tutoring marketplaces openly sell paid lead credits to tutors. That would be a legitimate paid service in the style of jr_15; it is not modelled here.

Distinct from jr_01 (agency fee for a guaranteed job): the recipient is a self-employed provider paying for leads, and the counterpart has a disclosed revenue share. Distinct from jr_14: there the legitimate fee is a fixed onboarding charge; here the legitimate model is a percentage of earnings only.
[N] is a proposed placeholder for a small integer (3–5).

evidence_references.claim: Upfront payment and unrealistic earning promises are red flags in fake job schemes (C11)
Fake recruiters ask for money in advance for "verification & registration" (CJ09)
